[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)

## **Why Recurring Billing Has a Different Cost Structure**


One-time payment gateway comparisons typically reduce to three variables: TDR, annual maintenance charge (AMC), and payment success rate. Recurring billing introduces three additional cost layers that most pricing page comparisons ignore entirely.


**Mandate registration fees** are charged by some gateways each time a customer authorises a new e-NACH or UPI Autopay mandate. At Rs. 5-15 per mandate, these costs compound quickly for businesses with high subscriber acquisition rates.


**Per-debit transaction charges** are the recurring billing equivalent of TDR on one-time payments. The rate is typically the same as the gateway’s standard TDR but is applied to every auto-debit event, not just the initial payment. A business with 1,000 active mandates executing one debit per month at Rs. 999/ticket is paying TDR on Rs. 9.99L/month in recurring GMV.


**Bounce handling costs** are the variable that most subscription businesses underestimate during vendor selection. When a debit fails because of insufficient funds, an expired mandate, or a bank-side rejection, gateways either pass through the NACH bounce fee (Rs. 350-500 per bounce charged by the originating bank), absorb it, or add a platform handling charge on top. At a 10-15% debit failure rate, common among consumer subscription businesses, these fees can materially erode the effective margin advantage of a lower TDR.


***Watch out:*** *A payment gateway charging 1.8% per-debit TDR with Rs. 449 bounce handling per failed mandate costs more per month than a 2% gateway with zero bounce handling overhead for businesses where debit failure rates exceed 9%.*


The correct evaluation framework for recurring billing is therefore not “which gateway charges the lowest per-debit TDR” but rather which gateway delivers the highest net realized revenue per rupee of subscription GMV billed after all mandate, debit, bounce, and maintenance costs are applied.


## **The TCO Formula for Recurring Payments**


**The Recurring Billing TCO Formula:** Net Realized Revenue = (Total Mandates x Debit Success Rate x Avg Ticket) – (Successful GMV x TDR) – (Failed Debits x Bounce Fee) – Monthly AMC


### **How We Evaluated**


This comparison is based on publicly available pricing data, gateway onboarding documentation, and merchant community reports as of June 2026. Where bounce fee terms were not disclosed on public pricing pages, figures are drawn from onboarding documentation and NPCI-mandated pass-through schedules. Debit success rate data is drawn from published benchmarks and gateway-disclosed figures. Mandate registration fees vary by plan tier and are noted accordingly.


### **Worked Example at 1,000 Mandates, Rs. 999/Month Average Ticket**


Monthly billing GMV = Rs. 9,99,000


**Payment Gateway A:** 2% TDR, 93% debit success rate, Rs. 0 AMC, Rs. 0 bounce handling fee


- Successful debits: 930 x Rs. 999 = Rs. 9,29,070
- TDR cost: Rs. 9,29,070 x 0.02 = Rs. 18,581
- Bounce handling: 70 failed debits x Rs. 0 = Rs. 0
- Net realized: Rs. 9,10,489


**Payment Gateway B:** 1.8% TDR, 85% debit success rate, Rs. 4,999/year AMC, Rs. 449 per bounce


- Successful debits: 850 x Rs. 999 = Rs. 8,49,150
- TDR cost: Rs. 8,49,150 x 0.018 = Rs. 15,285
- Bounce handling: 150 failed debits x Rs. 449 = Rs. 67,350
- AMC: Rs. 417/month
- Net realized: Rs. 7,66,098


Gateway A delivers Rs. 1,44,391 more per month in net realized subscription revenue at identical billing GMV. The 0.2 percentage point TDR advantage of Gateway B is immaterial against the combined drag of an 8-point lower debit success rate, Rs. 449/bounce costs, and Rs. 417/month in fixed AMC.


The break-even point on per-debit TDR alone (ignoring success rate and bounce costs) between a 2% zero-AMC gateway and a 1.75% Rs. 4,999/year gateway is approximately Rs. 2.08L/month in subscription GMV. Above that threshold, the TDR advantage begins to offset the AMC. But when debit success rate and bounce costs are factored in, the break-even shifts materially higher.

## **Cheapest Payment Gateway for Recurring Billing in India Reviews**


### **1. Razorpay**


**Parameter** **Value**


Per-Debit TDR 2% (standard)


UPI Autopay Support Yes


e-NACH Support Yes


Annual Maintenance Rs. 0


Setup Fee Rs. 0


Mandate Registration Fee Included (no separate charge)


Debit Success Rate 93%+


Bounce Handling Pass-through at cost (no platform surcharge)


Razorpay’s subscription billing product covers both e-NACH and[UPI Autopay](https://razorpay.com/upi-autopay/) under a single merchant dashboard, without requiring separate onboarding for each mandate type. The technical infrastructure includes intelligent retry logic that reschedules failed debits at statistically optimal times based on historical debit success patterns, which contributes to the reported 93%+ debit success rate across its merchant base.


For subscription businesses, the zero AMC structure is the most durable cost advantage at volumes below Rs. 5L/month in recurring GMV. There is no Rs. 3,600 or Rs. 4,999 annual charge sitting on top of the per-debit fee. Combined with a debit success rate approximately 6-8 percentage points higher than the category average, the TCO differential is significant from month one.


The 100+ supported payment modes mean Razorpay handles the initial subscription sign-up payment and the ongoing mandate debits on the same integration. Webhook infrastructure for debit events (success, failure, pending retry) is well-documented, which reduces engineering overhead for SaaS teams building dunning and collections logic on top.


Custom pricing is available for merchants exceeding Rs. 5L/month in recurring GMV, negotiated through the sales team. This is not advertised on the public pricing page but is a standard offering for mid-market and enterprise subscription businesses.


One honest limitation: the dashboard can feel feature-heavy for teams that only need the recurring billing module. Onboarding and support response times have been reported as slower during high-volume periods, which matters when a batch debit run fails at scale.


**Verdict:** The strongest total cost of ownership for subscription businesses processing under Rs. 5L/month in recurring GMV, driven by zero AMC, superior debit success rate, and no bounce surcharge.


**Best for:** SaaS, D2C subscription brands, and ed-tech platforms processing between Rs. 50K and Rs. 5L/month in recurring billing GMV.


### **2. CCAvenue**


**Parameter** **Value**


Per-Debit TDR 2% (standard)


UPI Autopay Support Yes


e-NACH Support Yes


Annual Maintenance Rs. 3,600/year (Rs. 300/month)


Setup Fee Rs. 0


Mandate Registration Fee Varies by plan


Debit Success Rate ~85%


Bounce Handling Pass-through; handling fees applicable


CCAvenue is one of India’s oldest payment gateways and carries that history in both its merchant footprint and its recurring billing product. The e-NACH infrastructure is mature and has been tested across insurance, utility, and lending use cases for over a decade. Enterprise merchants who require guaranteed bank-side support and existing relationships with public sector banks often find CCAvenue’s institutional standing more reassuring than newer alternatives.


The Rs. 3,600/year AMC is the primary cost drag for smaller subscription businesses. At Rs. 300/month, it adds a fixed overhead that makes the TDR-equivalent cost higher than it appears on the pricing page for any merchant processing under Rs. 1.2L/month in recurring GMV. The reported debit success rate of approximately 85% compounds this: at 1,000 mandates of Rs. 999/month, the 8-point success rate gap versus the market leader translates to 80 additional failed debits per month, each carrying bounce and retry overhead.


The UPI Autopay integration is functional but not as polished as the e-NACH product, which reflects the timeline of CCAvenue’s development roadmap.


**Verdict:** A credible option for established enterprises and regulated-sector businesses with existing CCAvenue relationships, but the AMC and lower debit success rate make it expensive at subscription volumes below Rs. 3L/month in GMV.


**Best for:** Enterprise merchants in insurance, utilities, or regulated lending who require institutional e-NACH infrastructure and have existing bank-side CCAvenue relationships.


### **3. Instamojo**


**Parameter** **Value**


Per-Debit TDR 1.7-2% (plan-dependent)


UPI Autopay Support Limited


e-NACH Support Limited (via partner integration)


Annual Maintenance Rs. 0 (free plan)


Setup Fee Rs. 0


Mandate Registration Fee Not disclosed publicly


Debit Success Rate ~80%


Bounce Handling Pass-through


Instamojo occupies the solopreneur and very-early-stage end of the Indian recurring billing market. Its zero-fee free plan removes the AMC barrier entirely, and for creators or service businesses running fewer than 100 active subscriptions, the simplicity of onboarding is a genuine advantage.


The limitations become significant at any meaningful subscription volume. The debit success rate of approximately 80% is the lowest among the gateways reviewed here, meaning 1 in 5 scheduled debits fails. For a business with 200 subscriptions at Rs. 999/month, that is 40 failed debits per cycle, each requiring manual follow-up or automated dunning infrastructure that Instamojo’s product does not natively provide in the same depth as dedicated subscription platforms.


The UPI Autopay support is limited compared to gateways where it is a first-class product. e-NACH is available but typically routed through a partner integration rather than native infrastructure. Businesses that anticipate growing past 300-400 active mandates within 12 months will likely find themselves re-platforming to a more capable gateway sooner than planned.


**Verdict:** Suitable for very early-stage subscription businesses below 100 active mandates where zero upfront cost and simple onboarding matter more than debit success rates and retry infrastructure.


**Best for:** Individual creators, coaches, and micro-SaaS founders running fewer than 100 active subscriptions with tickets below Rs. 500/month.


### **4. BillDesk**


**Parameter** **Value**


Per-Debit TDR Negotiated (not publicly disclosed)


UPI Autopay Support Yes


e-NACH Support Yes (institutional-grade)


Annual Maintenance Enterprise contract (not publicly disclosed)


Setup Fee Negotiated


Mandate Registration Fee Negotiated


Debit Success Rate ~88-90% (enterprise-tier)


Bounce Handling Negotiated SLA


BillDesk is not primarily a self-serve payment gateway; it is a payments infrastructure company with deep bank relationships and institutional NACH rails built over two decades. The PayU acquisition (completed 2023) has brought some modernisation, but the core value proposition remains the same: reliable, high-volume NACH processing for enterprise clients in regulated sectors.


Pricing is entirely negotiated. There is no public pricing page with standard TDR or AMC figures, which makes BillDesk impractical to evaluate for growth-stage businesses without a formal sales engagement. The minimum viable merchant profile is typically a regulated NBFC or enterprise processing hundreds of crores in annual recurring billing.


For that segment, debit success rates at enterprise tier (reported at 88-90%) and direct bank settlement relationships make BillDesk a strong technical choice for high-ticket mandates in insurance, mutual fund SIPs, and loan EMI collections.


**Verdict:** Not a practical option for growth-stage or self-serve subscription businesses. A serious consideration for regulated enterprises running Rs. 50 crore or more in annual recurring billing who need direct bank-side NACH relationships and negotiated SLAs.


**Best for:** NBFCs, insurance companies, mutual fund platforms, and enterprise lending businesses requiring institutional NACH infrastructure at high volume.


### **5. Stripe India**


**Parameter** **Value**


Per-Debit TDR 2% + Rs. 2 per transaction


UPI Autopay Support No (not natively supported)


e-NACH Support No (not supported)


Annual Maintenance Rs. 0


Setup Fee Rs. 0


Mandate Registration Fee N/A


Debit Success Rate ~90%+ (international cards)


Bounce Handling N/A (no mandate infrastructure)


Stripe India’s recurring billing infrastructure is built around international card subscriptions. As of June 2026, it does not natively support e-NACH or UPI Autopay, which are the primary recurring billing rails for domestic Indian consumers. Businesses requiring INR-denominated, bank-account-based recurring billing for Indian customers cannot use Stripe India as their primary recurring gateway.


Where Stripe India is useful for recurring billing is the inverse scenario: a global SaaS or platform billing Indian customers on international cards (Visa, Mastercard) in USD or INR. Stripe’s Billing product, webhook reliability, and dunning logic are strong for card-based subscriptions, and the developer experience is the best of any gateway reviewed here. For B2B SaaS selling to Indian enterprises who pay by card, it is a credible choice.


The absence of e-NACH and UPI Autopay is a structural limitation, not a pricing one.


**Verdict:** Not applicable for Indian consumer recurring billing via e-NACH or UPI Autopay. A strong choice for international card subscriptions and cross-border SaaS billing where Indian customers pay by card.


**Best for:** Global SaaS companies and B2B platforms billing Indian enterprise customers on international cards, where domestic mandate infrastructure is not required.


## **e-NACH vs UPI Autopay: Which Is Cheaper for Indian Subscription Businesses?**


e-NACH and UPI Autopay are the two primary recurring billing infrastructures in India, and they differ in ways that directly affect cost and operational complexity.


**Parameter** **e-NACH** **UPI Autopay**


Mandate registration method Bank form (physical/digital/net banking) UPI app (scan or link)


Registration friction Higher (3-5 business day processing for physical mandates) Lower (near-instant via UPI app)


Maximum debit limit Up to Rs. 1 crore/transaction Rs. 1 lakh per transaction (Rs. 15,000 for auto-debit without PIN)


Debit timing T+1 processing (bank business day) Near real-time


Failure/bounce fee source Bank-charged (Rs. 350-500); may be passed through Varies by gateway; typically lower


Best for High-ticket mandates (EMI, insurance premiums, Rs. 5,000+) Low-ticket, high-frequency, mobile-first subscriptions


Consumer adoption friction Higher (requires net banking or physical form) Lower (most Indian consumers have UPI on mobile)


For most SaaS, D2C subscription, and ed-tech use cases with average tickets below Rs. 2,000/month, UPI Autopay delivers better mandate registration conversion rates and near-instant confirmation. The lower per-bounce costs and faster registration make it the default starting point for new subscription businesses.


e-NACH remains the preferred infrastructure for high-ticket, bank-account-based mandates in lending, insurance, and mutual fund SIPs where transaction amounts exceed UPI Autopay limits or where the merchant requires debit on a specific calendar date regardless of network conditions.


Gateways that support both on a single integration reduce operational complexity. Merchants who must manage two separate gateway relationships for e-NACH and UPI Autopay carry a hidden overhead in reconciliation, reporting, and engineering maintenance.

## **Verdict: Which Gateway Is Right for Your Subscription Business?**


When evaluated on total recurring billing cost of ownership, including per-debit TDR, mandate registration overhead, debit success rates, bounce handling costs, and annual maintenance charges, the rankings shift considerably from what headline TDR figures suggest.


**For SaaS and D2C subscription brands processing Rs. 50K to Rs. 5L/month in recurring GMV:**


The combination of zero AMC, a 93%+ debit success rate, and bounce pass-through at cost makes one gateway the most cost-efficient option in absolute rupees for this segment. Custom pricing is available above Rs. 5L/month, which extends that cost efficiency to mid-market subscription businesses without requiring a change of infrastructure.


**For very early-stage subscription businesses under 100 active mandates:**


Zero-fee plan options with no setup cost remove the upfront barrier entirely. The trade-off is a lower debit success rate and limited mandate infrastructure, which becomes expensive as subscriber count grows.


**For regulated enterprises in lending, insurance, and financial services:**


Institutional NACH infrastructure with direct bank-side relationships and negotiated SLA terms is the primary requirement. Pricing transparency matters less at enterprise scale than operational reliability and regulatory alignment. Self-serve gateways are not the right product category for this segment.


**For global SaaS companies billing Indian enterprise customers on international cards:**


Domestic mandate infrastructure is not required. Card-based recurring billing with strong developer tooling and international dunning logic is the relevant evaluation criterion.


The variable that most subscription businesses underestimate at gateway selection is debit success rate. A 93% versus 80% debit success rate on 1,000 mandates of Rs. 999/month is the difference between Rs. 9,29,070 and Rs. 7,99,200 in successfully billed GMV per month, before TDR or fees are applied. No per-debit TDR comparison captures that Rs. 1.3L/month differential.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the TDR for recurring payments in India?**


Per-debit TDR for recurring billing typically mirrors the gateway’s standard transaction fee: 2% for most major gateways. Some gateways offer 1.75-1.8% at standard published rates, but the effective cost per successfully collected rupee also includes mandate fees, AMC, and bounce handling charges. Evaluating TDR alone for recurring billing systematically understates total cost by Rs. 417 to Rs. 5,000+ per month depending on the gateway and volume.


### **Is UPI Autopay cheaper than e-NACH for subscription billing?**


UPI Autopay generally carries lower bounce handling costs and faster mandate registration, making it more cost-efficient for low-to-mid ticket subscriptions (under Rs. 5,000/month average ticket) where consumer mobile adoption is high. e-NACH is better suited for high-ticket mandates above Rs. 5,000/transaction, regulated use cases in lending and insurance, and scenarios requiring guaranteed T+1 debit on a fixed calendar date. The gateway choice matters more than the mandate type: a gateway supporting both rails on one integration reduces reconciliation and engineering overhead.


### **Which payment gateway has the best recurring billing infrastructure in India for SaaS companies?**


For SaaS businesses in the Rs. 50K to Rs. 5L/month recurring GMV range, the relevant criteria are debit success rate, bounce retry logic, webhook reliability for dunning automation, and total cost of ownership. A gateway reporting 93%+ debit success rates with smart retry scheduling and zero AMC delivers materially more net realized subscription revenue per month than lower-TDR alternatives with lower success rates and maintenance charges. Custom pricing is available from most major gateways above Rs. 5L/month in recurring GMV.


### **Does recurring billing on Indian payment gateways carry an annual maintenance charge?**


Annual maintenance charges vary by gateway. Some charge Rs. 3,600/year, others charge Rs. 4,999/year, and some charge nothing. For a subscription business processing Rs. 2L/month in recurring GMV, a Rs. 4,999/year AMC adds Rs. 417/month in fixed cost, equivalent to a 0.21 percentage point increase in effective TDR. Gateways with zero AMC remove this fixed cost layer entirely, improving unit economics from month one.


### **What happens when a recurring debit fails? Who bears the bounce cost?**


When a scheduled auto-debit fails, the originating bank typically charges a NACH return fee of Rs. 350-500. Gateways handle this differently: some pass through the bank fee at cost, some absorb it into their pricing, and some add a platform handling charge on top of the bank fee. At a 10-15% debit failure rate, common in consumer subscription businesses, the difference between Rs. 0 and Rs. 449 per failed debit is a significant monthly cost. Gateways that pass through the bank fee at cost with no platform surcharge produce lower total bounce costs at scale.
